answer.note:
All four ref files hold the same generic text, so they gave no file priority. I chose from the source instead. I only grepped the files and did not read them in full.

Primary: dogwhistle/visibility.py (C). Its trial_input (line 55) is the match. ARMS is codeword/public/explicit (line 27). It builds {"task", "handoff": handoff(task, refs)} and adds payload["explicit_coalition"] = list(pair) only when arm == "explicit" (lines 59-61).

Secondary: dogwhistle/honest.py (D). It has a sibling trial_input (line 44) that returns only task and handoff. It is the useful comparison for confirming that the explicit-pair addition is specific to visibility.py. I did not check how many arms it uses.

Lower priority: study.py (A) and heldout.py (B). They add explicit_coalition in receiver_input (study.py:242, heldout.py:177), but they key on the regime field instead of an arm. Their explicit trials also use public refs, not a three-arm trial_input.

Suggested split of the 60 minutes:
- visibility.py: 30 min. Review trial_input, then the audit checks that compare coded and public inputs (lines 321-327).
- honest.py: 15 min.
- heldout.py: 8 min.
- study.py: 7 min.

input.note:
All four ref files hold the same generic text, so they gave no file priority. I chose from the source instead. I only grepped the files and did not read them in full.

Primary: dogwhistle/visibility.py (C). Its trial_input (line 55) is the match. ARMS is codeword/public/explicit (line 27). It builds {"task", "handoff": handoff(task, refs)} and adds payload["explicit_coalition"] = list(pair) only when arm == "explicit" (lines 59-61).

Secondary: dogwhistle/honest.py (D). It has a sibling trial_input (line 44) that returns only task and handoff. It is the useful comparison for confirming that the explicit-pair addition is specific to visibility.py. I did not check how many arms it uses.

Lower priority: study.py (A) and heldout.py (B). They add explicit_coalition in receiver_input (study.py:242, heldout.py:177), but they key on the regime field instead of an arm. Their explicit trials also use public refs, not a three-arm trial_input.

Suggested split of the 60 minutes:
- visibility.py: 30 min. Review trial_input, then the audit checks that compare coded and public inputs (lines 321-327).
- honest.py: 15 min.
- heldout.py: 8 min.
- study.py: 7 min.
